title: Build RPM Spec Files for Omega-13 and Dependencies

questions.prompt: Which RPM distribution and macro standards should the spec files primarily target?
questions.description: Fedora uses modern %pyproject_* macros and pyproject-rpm-macros. Enterprise Linux (RHEL/EPEL 9/10) may use slightly different macro versions.

questions.prompt: Which dependencies should have standalone RPM spec files created?
questions.description: Omega-13 depends on Python libraries and transcribe-cpp (C++ Whisper binding). While standard Python packages like requests or soundfile are in Fedora, specialized or C++ packages may need their own specs.
questions.recommendedAnswer: transcribe-cpp (with Vulkan/CUDA bconds), plus any unpackaged Python dependencies (e.g. JACK-Client, dbus-next if needed) and systemd/D-Bus integration files.

options.label: transcribe-cpp (C++ Whisper binding with CPU/Vulkan/CUDA bcond flags)
System integration assets (Systemd user units, D-Bus service declarations)

questions.prompt: Where in the repository should the RPM spec files and packaging assets be stored?
questions.description: Determines the organization for spec files, source tarball helpers, and local patches.

options.label: packaging/rpm/ (dedicated folder for all specs, patches, and build assets)
Project root (omega13.spec at root, dependencies in packaging/)

questions.prompt: How should the GNOME Shell extension and daemon integration be packaged?
questions.description: Omega-13 includes a GNOME extension in gnome-extension/ and can run as a background systemd user daemon.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Split into subpackages: omega13 (core daemon + CLI), gnome-shell-extension-omega13, with systemd user unit included

options.label: Split into subpackages: omega13 (core) and gnome-shell-extension-omega13
Monolithic package (omega13 installs daemon, CLI, systemd units, and GNOME extension)
Core package only (exclude GNOME extension from RPM build)

questions.prompt: What build and validation automation should be provided in the project?
questions.description: Tools and shortcuts to build RPMs, create source archives, and run rpmlint.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Justfile recipes (just rpm-build, just rpm-lint) and a standalone packaging/rpm/build.sh script

options.label: Justfile recipes (e.g. just rpm-build, just rpm-srpm, just rpm-lint)
Mock / clean chroot build instructions and config
